title: Executive summary - Las Vegas Strip single-entry poker trip
scope: Live tournament entries published on an official dated schedule inside the Las Vegas Strip walking corridor, filtered to one-day events whose official structure sheet was read and shows no rebuy, add-on or re-entry provision; plus the hotel cost side for the properties that can reach that poker room on foot.
method: Read the official schedule page in full (four page chunks), then read each referenced structure sheet in full and take only the values printed there. Cross-check: every guarantee in the event name had to match the guarantee on its sheet, and the build fails if it does not. Anything not published is blank and flagged, never filled in.
headline_numbers_note: Counts and the recommended window are injected from the generated datasets by scripts/build-site.py, so they cannot drift from the tables.

findings.title: One venue has a dated, per-event official source set - and it drives everything
findings.text: The Venetian's DeepStack Extravaganza IV (Nov 16 - Dec 23, 2026) publishes 64 numbered events as 94 rows with a structure sheet per event. No other Strip room in this dataset publishes a comparable dated document set, so the ranked table is Venetian-only and that limit is stated on every page rather than hidden.

findings.title: 46 one-day events have no re-entry, rebuy or add-on clause anywhere in their sheet
findings.text: All 37 official structure sheets were read in full (ten on 2026-11-16, 27 on 2026-11-17). 46 one-day rows across 19 sheets state no rebuy, add-on or re-entry clause. Each sheet lists a late-registration window and no additional-buy-in provision. That is the strongest state the published sources support - it is not a written single-entry guarantee (FG-02).

findings.title: The room does write re-entry rules when they exist - which makes the silence meaningful
findings.text: The PokerAtlas Valuetown sheet (events 18 and 58) states: 'PokerAtlas PRO players will receive a twenty ($20) rake discount on their initial $200 buy in only... All subsequent buy in's after the initial buy in will be $200.' Two consequences: those events allow further buy-ins, and a paid third-party membership lowers the first entry, which is a spending-based edge. Both are excluded from the single-entry table and shown separately.

findings.title: Multi-flight main events are not single-entry, by their own rule
findings.text: Event 01's sheet says each starting flight plays to about 12.5% of the field, Day 2 combines 1A-1D, and 'Any player who bags chips for Day 2 may not play a subsequent flight' - so an eliminated player may buy into another flight. All 28 flight rows (including the $800/$500K, $1,100/$150K, $1,100/$500K, $2,200/$1M and Seniors events) are therefore in the separate list, not the ranked one.

findings.title: A 'guarantee to buy-in' number worth using, and its limit
findings.text: The size ratio for the best verified rows: $600 into a $50,000 guarantee (83.3x, event 54, Dec 16), $600 into $40,000 (66.7x, events 28 and 30), $300 into $15,000 (50.0x, nine events). For bounty events the published guarantee explicitly includes total bounties, so the cash-only figure is smaller. The ratio describes the published guarantee per entry; it is not an expected value, and no field size is knowable in advance.

findings.title: The 8 AM start you asked for does not exist on this schedule
findings.text: Across all 94 rows the earliest start is 09:10 (a Dec 12 satellite) and the earliest cash-prize start is 10:10 AM. Long days are still available: 10:10 AM RaceDay Stack (registration closes 12:25 PM) followed by an 11:10 AM event the next day, or an 11:10 AM day event whose registration runs to about 4:55 PM. The only 9 AM recurring start found in any official Strip source is Horseshoe's.

findings.title: The hotel answer is currently a formula, not a price - because the room rate is the only missing term
findings.text: Verified from official pages: Venetian/Palazzo $55 resort fee plus tax and 13.38% Clark County room tax, $20/day guest parking, $150/night incidental authorization, $50/night per additional guest aged 13+, $100 plus tax for early checkout, and poker rates 'starting as low as $119 and $209'. Park MGM: $50 fee plus tax, $40 plus tax per extra occupant, $20/day parking, $100/day incidentals, 72-hour refundable first-night deposit. Wynn: $55 plus tax with free self-parking for two vehicles bundled in, $50 extra-guest surcharge, full-stay deposit at booking. Every booking engine renders date-specific prices only in JavaScript, so no nightly rate could be captured; the true cost is exact for fees and tax and open only on the rate.

findings.title: The cheapest entries quietly break the cheapest room rate
findings.text: The Venetian poker suite rate requires, each night, six hours of active live cash play or a $300-or-higher tournament buy-in, completed before 2 AM on the last night - otherwise 'your nightly suite rate will be adjusted to the prevailing rate'. A trip built from $200 RaceDay and $200 bounty events therefore forfeits the $119 rate. The plan builder prefers $300+ primaries for exactly this reason, and flags any day where it cannot.

findings.title: Walking time is unverified for every pair, and two facts do exist
findings.text: No official page publishes minutes. What is published: the poker room is inside the Palazzo (level 2, Grand Canal Shoppes) with in-resort directions from both the Venetian and Palazzo lobbies, and MGM's own page describes an interior bridge linking Bellagio, the Cosmopolitan and Vdara. So the Venetian and Palazzo are the only properties with a verified same-building route, and the 30-minute filter has no verified input for any other hotel.

findings.title: Ranking discipline applied
findings.text: Only rows with a confirmed fee and a confirmed guarantee are ranked (30 of 94). Eleven one-day rows are listed but unranked because their sheet has not been read; the remaining rows are satellites, tag-team, multi-flight, Day 2 restarts, final tables and the two partner-discount events. Bounty formats are labelled separately because their guarantee includes bounties.

recommendation.headline: Dec 6 - Dec 10, 2026 at the Venetian/Palazzo: four single-entry-candidate days, one event per day, evening events only as conditional fallbacks.
recommendation.why: It is the only four-consecutive-day window in the series where every day has a one-day event with a confirmed fee and guarantee, every primary is $300+ so the poker suite rate stays valid, and the average published guarantee-per-entry ratio is the highest of any such window (58.4x). Dec 13 - Dec 17 is the close alternative at 58.3x for $1,500 of entries instead of $1,800.

days.fallback: Event 29, $300 Bounty, 5:10 PM (enter only if out before 9:40 PM)

days.primary: Event 34, $300 Bounty, $15K GTD, 5:10 PM - this day has no verified morning start

days.fallback: none. Event 36 ($800 bounty, $75K GTD, 11:10 AM; sheet 16) is an alternative that day, not a fallback. Its sheet lists late registration to 4:55 PM and 30-minute levels, but no official source says how long a player lasts, so whether Event 38 (5:10 PM) can be reached after Event 36 is unknown and is not planned

recommendation.cost_model: 4 entries at $1,800 plus lodging at 4 x (rate + $55) x 1.1338. With the published $119 poker rate that is $197.28 per night, $789.12 for the stay, and about $2,589 before parking; add $80 if the $20/day guest parking applies (FG-07). Incidentals of $150/night are an authorization, not a charge.
recommendation.before_paying: Confirm in writing that Events 28, 30, 34 and 38 are limited to one entry (Q-03); read Event 36's sheet if you want the $800 (S-02); capture the itemised checkout total for Dec 6-10 (S-05); re-run the change monitor the morning you pay (S-10).
recommendation.not_claimed: Not a best-on-Strip claim: other rooms' schedules are not yet verified to the same standard. Not a forecast: no field sizes, no expected value, no finish times.

decision_sequence.text: Fix trip dates and nightly budget / quality floor
decision_sequence.detail: Dates: any 4-day window inside Nov 16 - Dec 23 is viable; Dec 6-10 is the best verified. Nightly ceiling and quality tier are not set, and no official quality rating exists (Q-02, FG-12).

decision_sequence.text: Get official structure sheets and written maximum-entry / no-rebuy / no-add-on rules; drop anything that fails the single-entry policy
decision_sequence.detail: 10 of 37 sheets read; 34 events pass on 'no contrary provision'; 28 flight rows, 7 satellites, 1 team event and the 2 partner-discount events are excluded by explicit text. The written confirmation itself is still outstanding (Q-03).

decision_sequence.text: Compare only the survivors on guarantee, buy-in, stack and blind duration, payout structure and schedule fit
decision_sequence.detail: All five fields are on the site per row, with excerpts; payout structure is '12.5% of the field' on every sheet read.

decision_sequence.text: Obtain itemised hotel totals for the same stay; check the walking route under 30 minutes
decision_sequence.detail: Fee, tax, occupant surcharge, parking, incidentals and cancellation windows are verified; the per-night rate is not, and no walk duration is verified (FG-05, FG-11).

decision_sequence.text: Build one event per day first; add evening events only where the earlier event can realistically be exited
decision_sequence.detail: 23 days carry one primary each; evening events appear only as conditional fallbacks gated by the later registration cutoff, with overlap flags computed from published times.

decision_sequence.text: Reconfirm official schedules, rates and policies before any non-refundable payment
decision_sequence.detail: A daily job re-reads every official URL and reports value-level changes; run it manually on the morning you pay.
